reviewText: This place is a must for any New Yorker... Pretty self explanatory, you absolutely have to try the pastrami!

I feel like speaking ill of such a renowned New York institution like Katz's is the equivalent of talking smack about your best friend's mother, but the sad truth is that I'm not a fan of this place. My first encounter here was a few years ago when I was in the neighborhood and needed a quick bite while waiting on line to see a show just up the street. A visit of mere minutes resulted in the purchase of a FIVE DOLLAR hot dog with zero frills. I love a hot dog and all, but honestly?  During a more recent trip, a group of friends had wanted to get together here, and I obliged, wanting to get the full Kat's experience. I know their giant sandwiches are their draw, but considering I wasn't even really hungry, paying $16 seemed out of the realm of logic. (I did check out the brisket sandwich my friend ordered, which looked rather dry, and wasn't anything he could rave about.) I decided to go for a spinach knish and a chocolate egg cream. The knish had no flavor beyond its exceedingly starchy taste. I didn't even bother to finish it. On the plus side, the egg cream was pretty delicious, but chocolate's hard to screw up. I can finally check Katz's off my bucket list but I don't really have a desire to return.
You have to go here if this is your first time in new york

heavy heavy heavy! delicious but super greasy/fatty pastrami!

This place is amazing, the food is beyond incredible.  The hot pastrami sandwich was so delicious, I would even say it was moderately priced at $15 a sandwich considering how tasty it was.  The service was pretty good by New York's standards.  Our waiter was attentive and friendly.  I'm not in New York often, but I know every time I'm in the area I will definitely stop at Katz.  Strongly recommend this restaurant.

The best DELI! World Wide. No one can come close to Katz Deli. The best Pastrami or LOKS. Their loks are amazing. Who doesn't like Smoked Salmon w/Cream Cheese, freshly made, on a freshly made bagel? Service is excellent and the price is on point especially for the amount of meat you get! Always a great spot to check out when you're in the city.
I love the pastrami sandwich! Don't eat all day til you go there!

Katz is awesome, the reason i gave it 4 out of 5 is because their prices are literally insane . . . but the food is great. Hey, spending $15 for sandwich every once in a while is ok I guess if the grub is out of this world - and it is!
Its really overrated and really expensive for a sandwich. Decor is crappy service waiters are really nasty

The pastrami on rye with a side of french fries, heaven! I love the guys that carve your meat too, they give you a slice while you are waiting and chit chat with you about everything and anything! You're not a New Yorker until you've been here!
All the tackiness and terrazzo are perfect decor for the warm, soft, spicy pastrami that melts through the rye.  The classic.  Don't tell me there is better pastrami in LA. It's a myth.
Obviously get the pastrami sandwich, but you should also try the matzo ball soup! Stay away from the Reuben which ruins the pastrami with too many toppings.
in the fast disappearing world of kosher or "kosher style" delicatessen, katz's remains -- and it's worth a visit and several bites.
Best deli in NYC
The experience is better than the food. Don't lose your ticket!
Top notch place for a great nosh xoxo

We arrived at Katz's at noon on a Saturday and I was tempted to walk away when I saw the huge line. My friends assured me that it was worth the wait, and I'm glad I trusted them. You have the option to be seated and served or order from the counter and find your own seat. Because there was a long wait to be seated, we decided to find our own table. It was kind of difficult "fighting" for a table, and once we did find a table, we were practically dining with the party next to us. Once I tasted the pastrami on rye, I didn't care if the person next to me was sitting in my lap. It was the best sandwich I have ever eaten. This is a definite must try when in NYC!

okay, we went on recommendation of friends... not realizing it was the famous "i'll have what she's having" movie place, until weeks later... a long walk from the metro... what a dump... and not nearly as good, nor clean, as canter's in l.a., but worth a visit to soak up some new york kulture.
TOO MUCH CONFUSION..I ALSO DON'T LIKE BEING A "NUMBER" EXPECIALLY FOR MEDOCHRE FOOD!

I grew up in the LES so I never really thought of this place as a landmark until  I got to HS. It's when the lines started happening outside of this establishment.  I didn't get an opportunity to try this place until I moved out of the neighborhood but many of my friends worked there and raved about it.  The food here is amazing, make sure to get a meat product.  It has an old school diner feel to it, with references to the movie when Harry Met Sally (they have that table).  Great food in an amazing location. Must check it out.
The best corned beef and pastrami in the City, although you have to fight the crowd to order it.
Great sandwiches. Huge. Really huge. Also, really expensive.

Best pastrami in New York! But other than the delicious food this is a unique experience to order food. You get your ticket, try some fresh cut samples, then get 2 sandwiches on rye: the pastrami and the corn beef. Just try both if your a first timer. They are expensive but totally worth it. It's like the caviar of meat.
Pastrami. Fries. Good luck.

Straight tourist trap. These sandwiches cost more than they are worth. Their montreal rival, schwartz, is the perfect version of this place. The sandwich tastes good, dont get me wrong, but they are not worth what they sell them for at all. If it was a $8 or $9 sandwich, i understand, but the meat isn't THAT good to charge $18 for a Reuben? No, that doesnt make sense, the sandwich is not even that big, its a regular sandwich, that could easily be mistaken for a more fancy version of the reuben you get at Lenny's or something.  Not worth it, save your money, they are probably charging that much because their location's rent is very high. who knows, but not worth a visit.
best deli in the city.  institution on houston street.

I wish I could enjoy Katz's more. It's a city landmark (in reputation, at least,) it's open very late into the night in a very late-night kind of neighborhood, and the food is not something that you can get everywhere. However, the unorganized nature of the place is a little off-putting. Do you go to a counter? Which one do I get the pastrami at? Why is there a group waiting to be seated, but the place is mostly empty?  That guy just grabbed a sandwich and seated himself!  Yes, Katz's is an experience. It's also very expensive, even more so than most other kosher-style delis in the city. The meats are very fatty, more than they traditionally should be. Lastly, it's cash-only.
Good shit!
The best Corned Beef and Pastrami in the city bar none.  Unique ticket system and decor.  One of a kind.
it never lives up to the memories, but it's still worth going to
Server was rude at first, then just sarcastic

It's a great place for pastrami sandwiches, but not much else. I don't think most of the food items they offer are all that great. If you can, sit at the table where Meg Ryan and Billy Crystal filmed "When Harry Met Sally."

Corned Beef! Pastrami! Shame on you if you've never had the pastrami or corned beef here. New Yorkers will ignore the whole When Harry Met Sally thing here, but it's alright if you ask for what she's having.

Ridiculous pastrami, and definitely worth visiting for. One of the most unique eating experiences I have had!  I see many reviews mentioning this place as expensive. To be fair, I didn't notice it. But then I may be too used to London prices.

I've never sat down at the service side of the restaurant, only the side which requires you to stand in line and order.  This is initially confusing, but the lines move quickly and the guy who makes your sandwiches is quick and responsive.  Tip a dollar or two at the counter.  Stick with the Pastrami sandwich, which will make you realize why Pastrami could be worthy of love.
The best pastrami sandwich in the city! Delicious, crunchy pickles! Don't lose your ticket, they'll never let you leave.
share sandwiches, too much for one.
The pastrami sandwiches are huge!  We usually split one between two people.
Whats with kats? you pay $20 bucks and feel like your on a lunch line in jail!  i'd pass on that.  Try This little piggy!
so expensive for bad food
This is a very famous place and you should check it out at least once.
The layout of the deli is horrible and a mess, the bathrooms were worse than a truck stop, and being proud of being rude does not make you clever, it just makes you rude.

Yes, it's an icon, much praised and much beloved by most.  I thought the pastrami and corned beef were incredibly greasy, and the cheesecake was not nearly as dense or tasty as I expected. Plus it's quite expensive for what it is. Not for me.

It's low-frills and packed with people, but Katz's has the best deli food in town. Not just tourists, locals also head here with frequency. So, shove your way to the front of the counter for the best pastrami on rye in Manhattan.
Mmm, the pastrami is amazing!

This place is definitely a bit of a touristy trap, so actually getting in and funding a seat is an adventure. That said, the pastrami is probably the best I've ever eaten. Totally worth it.
The food was great, the atmosphere was wonderful and the staff is awesome. Hope to visit more often
AMAZINGLY AWESOME
This is a NYC institution. Good place to bring the folks from outta town. Show them the real NY. Big sandwiches and you'll pay for 'em.

Loved the food. Some low reviews say it was expensive. I am glad no one came up to the table and asked for more money because i would have gave it to them. Well worth it plus some.  Oh the pickles. I have yet to eat some as good.  I wonder if they ship them to the midwest...
BEST pastrami.  Wish I still lived 2 blocks away.  Well, maybe that was dangerous.

The Good - Food is delicious. So far I have tried; chilli dogs and the reuban sandwich w/ pastrami. The macaroni salad was tasty but I do not think they make it there. It tasted like the Sally Sherman macaroni salad that is commonly sold in supermarkets.   The Bad - Usually very busy. You can sit down and have waiter service or you can wait for your food at deli counter and then bring it to your seat. We usually get waiter service and haven't had an issue getting a table quickly. If you wait for your food the line is usually long and you have to go to different stations to get the various things you want.  Complaint - Apparently waiter service ends at 10:00pm on some nights. We sat down at 9:40pm. The waiters would not even look in our direction. We are pretty sure that they did it on purpose so that they wouldn't get stuck serving us until closing.   At first we figured it was just busy. However, after 25 minutes of having the waiters fly by us it was evident that we were being ignored and we went up and ordered our food.  Very annoying!! The waiters could have just informed us that they were no longer taking orders at the table instead of letting us sit there.   TIP: Hold on to your ticket. They write down how much you owe and you pay on your way out. If you lose the ticket, they will make you pay $50. They also have bouncers to enforce this rule.   Decor: This place is very old school. On the walls there are tons of pictures of celebrities who have visited. If you sit at tables with waiter service  then the tables are private. If you sit in the self-serve area then anyone can sit next to you.
WELL LETS SAY IT WAS A GREAT DAY I ALWAYS WANTES A CORN BEEF SANDWICH AND PICKLES .
I absolutely love this place, I never ate pastrami until I visited this place and it was wonderful.
The classic Jewish deli. Rivals the best in Montreal. The pastrami is what you should order, and the pickles are a nice touch. Loved it.

The pastrami on rye really is excellent . . . but so is the reuben sandwich, the corned beef sandwich, the brisket sandwich, the knockwurst with beans, the cheese steak, the homemade beef stew, the potato latkes, the split pea soup . . . .  Yes. I've been to Katz's more than a few times. Whenever I am anywhere near the place, I usually stop in. If you've never had a knish, this delicatessen's knishes are well worth losing your virginity for.
go for the pastrami and fatty corned beef.

BEST PASTRAMI ANYWHERE..... cut by hand. Natural casing all beef hot dog the same as Nathan's and terrific........same as Papaya King and Grey's too but this one bigger. Nothing has changed here since they ordered the sign and told the sign painter to write "Katz's" that's all....and he wrote "Katz's That's All"........there you go, a little bit of history

The pastrami is enough to keep me coming back time after time but don't miss out on the corned beef as well.  This is a certified Adam Richman (Man Vs. Food) pig out place and that is good enough for me!
Never got the appeal of Katz. The sandwiches are good, but the lines are always long and it's always crowded. Don't lose your ticket!

Service is excellent and the price is on point especially for the amount of meat you get! Always a great spot to check out when you're in the city.

I love the spinach knishes. If you need to use the bathroom it is in the back and it is TINY! Haha, you can't eat the food and fit in that bathroom but when you gotta go, you gotta go.

I get a sandwich here once in awhile and it is good. no complaints here. got to tell them exactly what you want though because they cant read your mind. cool dudes

I love the people who complain about the food here.  They do so because they have no idea what good deli food was in the past and still is at very few places.  These are the same folks who would eat in Italy and complain that the food was not as good as Olive Garden.  If you eat there you WILL NOT leave hungry.  Great food....amazing atmosphere.

It's good, but I'm not sure Katz's lives up to the hype. It kind of feels like a tourist trap.   The pastrami is sliced thick, and it IS very good, but the brisket came out a little dry. Our chicken noodle soup felt very pedestrian. I feel that I got much better value from 2nd Ave. Deli.   It is cool to be in the middle of a lot of history though. With photos of celebrities ringing the dining room, salamis hanging from the walls, and an old-timey water fountain in the back, you get a great atmosphere and tradition. That, and this place's legend, will keep packing 'em in.
Worst service ever. Good pastrami, underwhelming Philly cheesesteak.
you should know what you are getting into it a trip

The owner came to my table and personally spoke with me about my food. He then gave me a sample of pastrami as I had ordered the corned beef. Giant Sandwiches. Wish I could get 1/2 Corned Beed 1/2 Pastrami to try them both...
What happens when you don't get the pastrami? food poisoning. I got the philly steak, not a happy ending. The pastramis didn't look that special anyway.
Forget the sandwiches, they are too big unless you are spliting with at least 3 people. Get the latkes, blintzes and an egg cream!
Very good food but unfriendly staff
Delicious food, but Staff not so friendly...

We sat in the "Waiter Service" section late on a weeknight.  It was busy, and the service was pretty slow, The waitress seemed disorganized and forgetful, but friendly.  Please note, we didn't receive an itemized bill, so we weren't sure if gratuity was included.  This made tipping confusing.  Food was excellent, if a little pricy.  Nonetheless, we enjoyed our experience at Katz's.
old time favourite, one sandwich could feed half a village... and don't forget the pickles!

Love this place! everything is delish....it can get really busy! I would recommend their pastrami sandwich and matzo ball soup yummy!!   i love bringing my tourist friends here and taking pics under the 'O' sign (when harry met sally) =)

It's a classic! You have to go here if you are visiting NYC. Typical New York deli style food with real New Yorkers. The Rueben is a good one, sauerkraut you have to have and pickles. The place is also famous for the "When Harry Met Sally" orgasm scene. :p
where else can you get that pastrami on christmas day.
The best deli meats in the city in their overstuffed sandwiches!
I'll have what she's having...which includes: latkes, half sour pickles, half pastrami sandwich and matzo ball soup. Don't forget the chopped liver!
Best pastrami sandwich I've ever had! It's fairly price (about $15/sandwich) but it's worth every dollar! Must try when in Manhattan!
Squeeze by the tourists and the food is good with a lot of meet.  The process is a minor step above chaos.  The staff is cooperative

There is a method to the madness and it's called Katz's Delicatessen.    It has attitude. It has crowds. It has pastrami.  I will always look for a place to compare with Katz's where ever I travel, but I will never find quality pastrami sandwiches like Katz's.  Their corned beef is also to die for.  Know what you want before heading in and you'll be fine.  Be aggressive, but don't be a dick and have fun!  I don't think you can go wrong with the food here.  Keep in mind the prices are up there.  Try the pastrami with some cream cheese on the side.  It's good.  The service counter where you pick up your drinks may look at you crazy, but trust me it's good otherwise I wouldn't be telling you!  Tell them Jerry sent you!  Pros * Pastrami to die for * Portions * Taste  Cons * Cost * Crowds  Review date: 10/15/2008

Food wasn't anything to rave about. weird system that wasn't explained when going in. get a ticket, go to the counter, order your food, they write what you bought on the ticket and when you leave the cashier chargers you. On my way out though I noticed there was a full service section which is what I wanted in the first place! Staff was a little rude too. Cash only which you don't find out until you're already at the cashier. Weird experience in general.

total bust for vegetarians.
Over priced and below average food. I had a pastrami and it was super greasy that sat on my chest the whole night n prevented me from enjoying my night
Ein muss für jeden Liebhaber von Sandwich, Burger und Co. Ein echt interessantes Lokal -> must see!
Pastrami not as good as one would hope.

These sandwiches are huge. After you get in be prepared to wait. Don't lose your ticket or they throw a fit. It's easier to eat if you separate into 4 pieces of meat-topped toast so everything doesn't fall out. Dislike how you only get tiny glasses of water and have to keep walking back there for more.

Old School, Place to Share. Try something like the half brisket, half pastrami and some deli pickles ordered from one of the no nonsense deli guys (but they will let you try a sample of the meat options if you ask) and some specially brewed katz's ale from brooklyn brewery and sit down to share both with a friend. Not cheap, fun to have every so often
Horrible, rude service.  Confusing order system.
14 bucks for a pastrami sandwich.  Great experience, but perhaps once is enough.
Food is good, but wait is long and the prices are good.
Best reuben pastrami on rye in NYC
a happening
Don't go when they are cleaning the floor and don't lose your ticket. This place is famous and as most famous places get, overrated.

Vu le prix que ça coûte ils pourraient refaire la déco, ça doit être l'endroit le mieux amorti de la ville... si au Mac do ils retirent leur burger après un laps de temps, ici c'est une fois que ce laps de temps est écoulé qu'on vous sers votre sandwich infâme. Where else can you get a heaping portion of pastrami that tastes so damn good? A little expensive and cash only, but you get what you pay for!
Best pastrami around...
NYC landmark.  Pricey but worth it.
Okay, yes, it's a tourist trap. But man do they have some tasty pastrami. ::drool:: If you've never tried it, go.
Good food, but expensive for what it is.
Great food
Disappointed.  Greasy food. Overpriced. Feels like a factory rather than a restaurant. Try carnegie instead.
Best. Pastrami. Ever. Other stuff on the menu is great too but definitely try the pastrami first.
Poor quality pastrami and pickles. Very high prices: double what they should be.

This probably the best example of traditional delicatessen food in New York City. There's a reason Katz's is world famous. The pastrami on rye was excellent. I would recommend going here once a while as a treat, but not regularly. The prices don't support that kind of habit.
Killer corned beef but overrun by tourists.  Get your meal to-go.
großartiges essen, nur etwas teuer... aber sehr zu empfehlen!

Kat'z.  The dream of reliving what the LES once was.  Too bad the dream turned into a nightmare.  First of all, for a restaurant to have hired security is quite ridiculous, especially a Jewish deli.  The security were extremely rude and all they would do is yell at you though really they should have been taking care of crowd control because it was a total mess of people inside not sure where to go.    The ordering system makes sense once you have been there once, but as a first-timer (even though I grew up in NY, I never went until now) it was confusing especially with the hordes of people inside.  Huge fire hazard as well.  The ticket system is not too efficient and it is not explained well as you enter the restaurant.  As a party of three, we were given three tickets, though we thought we would only need one because we are paying all together.  This got us into a lot of trouble at the end when security would NOT LET US LEAVE even though we had a receipt, because we were missing two of our tickets.  This is when the situation got ugly.  The security were extremely unprofessional to everybody in my party, using sarcasm and mocking tones.  They told us that we can go ahead and call the police but it would be a waste because they would be against us.  We basically became prisoners unable to leave the restaurant even though we had proof we paid.  Ultimately we had to find the manager and explain what happened.  He acted like he was doing us a huge favor to have us escorted out.    The food was good, very good.  The knishes were some of the best I've ever had.  But, I can go to Ben's and have a much more enjoyable experience without the crazy security and the food is on par with Kat'z (and cheaper).

so looking forward to try them after reading all the good reviews, but it was a total disappointing experience. The door bitch kept yelling at customers like they were prisoners, kept pushing them in, giving them "tickets" nobody knows what we are supposed to do with them. it was just a mess!! do i stand here? do i wait for a table here? do i buy the sandwich here? totally confused and still kept being yelled at. some people just couldn't stand it and left, we tolerated it and would like to find out what the fuss was about. when we finally got our table (had to fight for it they kept missing our name), it was a tiny table sharing with other people. the meat was over cooked and so unbelievably dry, i couldn't finish the second half, then they missed our order we didn't get the fries, i was actually glad at that point it didn't come out because I just wanted to leave, I just couldn't move got stuck between the tables. do we pay at the table? at the door? after sitting there for 10 mins trying to look for a staff, i was glad it was finally finished, paid and out of the door. Then the door bitch chased out yelling again "hey where is your ticket? " I told him I already gave it back, not a word of "thank you", just a filthy look at me like i stole his stupid ticket. get rid of the stupid confusing ticket system, and start treating people like people. will definitely not going back, what a waste of time. If only I could give less than 1 star.
Tourists sometimes get in the way; but still the best pastrami ever
The absolute best Old School NYC deli. This is a must for any lover of pastrami.
Greatest remaining Deli!
Been going here for over 50 years.  Nothing has changed, but my arteries are thicker.  Even the waiters are the same.
A NYC Must see.  Heaven if you love pastrami. Make sure you get the fries.
Still the best Jewish deli in New York.
huge sandwiches and a NYC institution
besides being a landmark any neighborhood deli does it better

The famous Katz's best pastrami in manhattan. Its expensive but so very worth it! Workers are very friendly, while you wait for your order your given a taste, always busy lines are long but moves fast. The walls are covered with pictures of famous people from actors to singers many more. If your in the area stop by see for your self.
Amazing place,and the beef are so delishes ;) Sure u have to wait a time,but it makes sense ;)
Pastrami with swiss and sourkrout! Delicious!
The best corned beef sandwich on the lower east side, I highly recommend this spot if you thirst for a great corned beef on rye.

This old Jewish deli is has some of the best corned beef and pastrami sandwhiches In all of ny. It is a stop every tourist should go to for a true taste of a old school new York deli. You should also get the kinish and a celray (celery soda), they are also new York staples. The food is way over priced but worth every dollar. You won't be dissapointed.
Ottima la carne con il Pastrami . Ma se bi fate servire al tavolo i prezzi salgono alle stelle .

"Borscht Belt" dining doesn't get more "authentic" than at this LES Jewish deli that's been supplying "skyscraping" pastrami and corned beef sandwiches since 1888; true, it's "cash only" with "low-frills" decor and service, but ultimately it's a "completely NY experience", best known for the immortal line ‘I'll have what she's having' from When Harry Met Sally.
Very delicicious sandwiches. Great if you are hungry.  But maybe not the place for a romantic date.
Una tradizione Newyorchese. ... ottimo il pastrami

I can't even begin to tell you how long this place has been here. The best way to get in and even get a seat is to come at a time when there aren't many tourists, especially if you're a local or a native new yorker. Food service here is excellent, and I know for a fact that they hire people from the neighborhood such as school students from the area.

The Pastrami was amazing here! Easily worth the 15 bucks they are charging. If you've never been here, when you first enter they hand each person a ticket. This is how they keep track of what you've bought. Go up to the different sections of the counters to get the food/drinks/sides you want and hand the person helping you your ticket. When you leave they will charge you. This system is awesome and it makes for a quick moving line. If you are in NYC you definitely have to come here!!!
Awesome sandwiches

I go to Katz's for the pastrami,for the hot dogs, for the fries, and for the  Dr. brown's Cel-Ray soda. I'm sure the rest of the food is good, but for over  50 years I eat A Pastrami on rye, fries ( or sometimes potato salad), a hot dog and a soda.Katz's cn not be compared to anywhere else. it's a one of a kind deli!

This is truly the place to go in NYC for a real deli experience. The reuben sandwich is my fave. My little brother always asks to get a corned beef sandwich from here every time he visits from the Midwest. He says "you just can't get a sandwich like this back home...."
Perfect in every way imaginable. Anyone who complains otherwise must be a backwards communist.

[EN] I was expecting more, I took the pastrami sandwich and there was nothing but meat... a sandwich needs at least 2 different ingrediets + sauce! And it is overpriced for my opinion. Also the air conditioner is too powerful, I was really freezing in there!  [IT] Mi aspettavo molto di più, ho preso il pastrami sandwich e c'era solo carne... un panino deve avere almeno 2 ingredienti e una salsa, altrimenti che razza di panino è?! E costa anche decisamente più del dovuto a mio avviso. Inoltre l'aria condizionata è da pazzi, mi stavo congelando là dentro!
Love the food I just get overwhelmed with the larg crowd. But that wont stop me from going once a month.

Everyone must experience Katz's Deli at least once. We go every time we are in NYC. The lines can be quite long at lunch and it is a bit confusing for first-timers as they don't really tell you how to order and the counter ordering area can be hectic and overwhelming. Just stand in line, tell them what you want and they will give you a sample of the meat. You give them your ticket and they right down the charge, You have to go to a separate line to order drinks, french fries, potato salad, etc. I always order this after the sandwich is made because this line is super fast and you don't want your fries to get cold! The prices will knock your socks off...about $18 for a pastrami on rye. The fries are another $5 or $6.... BUT-- the portions are HUGE. We are good eaters but always share a sandwich and one order of fries. Knowing this, it brings the total cost to a more reasonable level. They only accept cash-- so, be aware of that, too. The place is filled with tons of pictures of celebrities-- very cool to look at. One day, there just maybe someone famous there when we visit! Highly recommend-- you will never eat better pastrami!

My husband and I decided to try Katz Deli because we saw how well it was ranked on Zagat.  As we walked by, there was a line which we thought was a promising sign that this would be amazing! Not too long after getting in line we were allowed to go inside.  Instead of being welcomed by a host or hostess we were forcefully directed by a security guard in uniform who was throwing his hands around and behaving aggressively towards the patrons. We finally saw a guy taking names for Waited service and we got our name down. We waited for 25 minutes by a trash can, crowded by people also waiting for tables and being shoved by yelling employees pushing carts with dirty dishes.  A lady went up to the hotdog counter while we stood there and asked for a grilled cheese and fries.  She was told fries are down there and he pointed and then he said you have to wait 10 minutes for us to start your grilled cheese because the grill is cold.  She asked if there was a way to get everything in one place and he replied,"No, you can't.  Look at this place lady!" It was a terrible experience waiting for the table, but we expected the food to make up for it.  Our name was called and we were seated.  Walking back we looked at the plated food and our optimism returned.  Our waiter had a pleasant personality. I ordered a Reuben and my husband ordered a Philly Cheesesteak.  They looked delicious!  The relish and sauerkraut was delicious on the reuben!  The meat was absolutely disgusting! It tasted like Dog Food.  The Philly tasted like bland cheap hamburger and we had to put a ton of salt and pepper on it just to get something good out of it.  The food is not awful overall, but not great and definitely not worth the hassle of waiting and being mistreated. The experience and the restaurant reminded us of Carnegie Deli which has equally become a crazy tourist attraction rather than something that delivers on it's promise.   We gave it a chance, and we will not return.

Food:   I give  B+ for the meat and C for the rest.  Pastrami is of course much better than you would normally get in a New York deli or diner.  It is a bit too fat for my taste but many people may like it that way. Excellent texture.  Flavor is good.   The rye bread is OK but could be much better.   Bread can and does make all the difference for sandwiches.  Coleslaw is a mayo drenched junk.  Pickles are below average.  Mustard is mild, sweet, and cheap just as in any diner.  Warning: order one sandwich for two people unless you weigh over 200 lbs or plan to be in the near future. Save money too.  Atmosphere: At 2 pm there were 20 people outside in line which moved fast.  Once in, it is very disorienting.  Someone shoves tickets in your hand and tells you to get on one of several lines. But the lines are merged into a swarming crowd like it is a rush hour at Grand Central.   Then you stare for 5 minutes at a wall of choices to order, not wanting to make the wrong choice, i.e. take the wrong train.   Ticket is marked by the sandwich maker to show what you are getting when handing the food over to you on a tray. It looks like mayhem, until you settle down at one of the tables and realize that ordering food here is overwhelming only the first time around. A Must Do on the "What Touristy Thing Can I Take My Out of Town Relatives To?" list.  It's like going back in time. Hand-painted signs. Plastic lettered menu boards. An endless wall of Celebrity Photos. Formica tables. And an ordering system that confuses locals and tourists alike. All that's missing is cigar smoke. Oh, and they only take cash. Just like the good 'ol days.  Here's a short primer. I still might get it wrong because I screwed up the whole thing myself. But it wasn't that busy and no one yelled at me, so it was all good.   Get your ticket.  Hold onto your ticket.  Do not lose your ticket.   Find a counter guy that isn't inundated with customers. But don't go down the line too far or you'll end up in the Waiter Service Only section. Once you place your order, you will be given multiple tastes of meat.   Do yourself a favor and just order the Pastrami. It's what they're know for, and if you don't, you'll regret it until the end of your days. Now wouldn't be a bad time to put a dollar or two into the tip jar. Get more scrumptious pieces of pastrami. You will get complimentary pickles and cucumber spears. All the condiments are at the table so don't worry about that just yet.  Now the counter guy will ask for and mark up your ticket. The markings won't make a bit of sense to you, so don't worry about it. Just don't lose it! There's no way you're going to sneak out without paying, so just get that thought out of your head right now.   Look up and read the signs. The tables along the Wall of Celebrities are Waiter Service Only. There's a sign right above the "When Harry Met Sally" table, so you don't have to ask.   I ordered the Half Pastrami sandwich and a bowl of Split Pea Soup. The soup needed something. So, I put almost half my pastrami sandwich in it. Delicious! Pastrami really gives ham a run for it's money. I could go completely Halal if I could get me some good pastrami on the regular. Easy.   Once you're done, just leave your tray on the table. There are a bunch of roaming busboys to clear it away.  Now, where's your ticket? You left it on the tray didn't you?  Take your ticket and pay cash for your delicious and filling meal. Tip the cashier as well. What? Why not? She can read that mysterious ticket and didn't overcharge you. Give her a buck.
